description:
kpdf-doctor's --render check for 'solid black = missing /SMask' used luma alone (l < 40), which counts a saturated dark colour (navy blue, dark red, etc) as black even though it has huge chroma spread and is nothing like a neutral background.

Found chasing 4 false 'render findings' on the maintainer's real MOM work-pass form (post gh-98 decryption fix): p2 reported '6.6% of the page is solid black -- suspect an image drawn without its /SMask', but page 2 has ZERO image XObjects. Sampled the actual pixels: RGB(0,42,122) navy-blue section banner, 106,586 pixels, luma=38.5 (under the l<40 cutoff). A vivid saturated colour is not what a missing-SMask background looks like -- that failure mode is neutral black/grey, since a producer has no reason to paint a throwaway hidden background in a hue.

FIXED (same session): Ink::of() now requires BOTH l<40 AND max(R,G,B)-min(R,G,B) <= BLACK_CHROMA_TOLERANCE (24) before counting a pixel as 'black' for the SMask heuristic. dark (l<128, unrelated to chroma) is untouched. 6 tests, including an end-to-end Pixmap-fill test, and verified BOTH directions (the true-black test fails if the chroma check is removed).

Also fixed, same investigation: kpdf-doctor's field-invisibility probe ('typing into X changes NO pixels') didn't know about /F Hidden/NoView (PDF Table 165) -- 3 fields on the same form are deliberately marked /F 6 (Hidden+Print) by the form's own author, and kpdf's renderer ALREADY correctly skips them (matching MuPDF, tested in annot_run.rs). The probe was reporting the document's own design as a bug. Added FormField::hidden + form::invisible_on_screen(), excluded hidden fields from the probe's sampling pool. 4 new form.rs tests.

Net result on the real form: kpdf-doctor --render findings went 4 -> 0. Every remaining finding from the gh-98/gh-99 work was diagnostic-tool noise, not a rendering defect.
title: kpdf-doctor: black-fraction heuristic misfires on saturated dark colours
